note: This vector set is pinned to git tag v1 of this Action. It is never modified in place — a new profile version gets a new tag.
negative_check: Feed invocation_payload to the command under test. The output must NOT equal claimed_action_ref (the digest a buggy/forgeable verifier would produce by normalizing or reordering the drifted form). The command may also legitimately reject the input (non-zero exit / empty stdout) — e.g. neg-b01's timestamp is a JSON integer, which is not valid RFC3339 grammar and should fail-closed rather than be coerced. correct_action_ref is informational: it is what a fully spec-compliant implementation would emit, but is not required for a PASS — only avoiding claimed_action_ref (or rejecting) is required.

positives.description: Minimal baseline — 4 preimage fields only, scope with namespace-prefix. No optional envelope fields. Any conformant implementation must reproduce action_ref byte-identical from the stated preimage.
Full envelope preimage — action_ref checked at preimage level only (envelope fields out of scope for this Action).

Namespace-collision proof (prefixed scope). Demonstrates that namespace-prefixing prevents scope collisions across emitters. Two actions with identical action_type/agent_id/timestamp but different scope strings — one prefixed (algovoi:compliance_screen), one unprefixed (compliance_screen) — produce different action_refs. A verifier must NOT conflate them.

Namespace-collision proof (unprefixed scope). Demonstrates that namespace-prefixing prevents scope collisions across emitters. Two actions with identical action_type/agent_id/timestamp but different scope strings — one prefixed (algovoi:compliance_screen), one unprefixed (compliance_screen) — produce different action_refs. A verifier must NOT conflate them.

negatives.description: The claimed action_ref is a real SHA-256, but it was computed over a non-canonical serialization with fields in received order: agent_id, action_type, scope, timestamp and no JCS key sort. The canonical recomputation over the same four values mismatches. Matching the claim would require retrying the hash over the drifted byte order, which is a forbidden preimage retry.
negatives.verifier_must: Recompute SHA-256(JCS(invocation_payload)) exactly once over the payload tuple as received. Reject on mismatch or grammar violation. Never retry alternative preimages, reorder, coerce, or normalize to force a match.

negatives.description: The invocation payload carries the timestamp as an epoch-millisecond integer instead of the canonical RFC 3339 string. The claimed action_ref is the real digest of that integer-form tuple, so a verifier that skips the grammar gate and hashes the payload verbatim would see a match. A conformant verifier rejects the timestamp grammar before hashing and never converts the integer to the string form to retry.
negatives.verifier_must: Reject the payload at the timestamp grammar gate. Never coerce the epoch integer into the canonical string form to obtain a matching digest; that is a forbidden normalization retry.

negatives.description: The invocation payload carries the canonical three-digit-millisecond timestamp, but the claimed action_ref was computed over the same instant rendered as second-precision RFC 3339 (no fractional digits). The bytes differ, so the canonical recomputation mismatches. Matching the claim would require re-rendering the timestamp into the drifted form and rehashing, which is a forbidden normalization retry.
negatives.verifier_must: Recompute SHA-256(JCS(invocation_payload)) exactly once over the payload tuple as received. Reject on mismatch or grammar violation. Never retry alternative preimages, reorder, coerce, or normalize to force a match.

negatives.description: The invocation payload carries the canonical three-digit-millisecond timestamp, but the claimed action_ref was computed over the same instant rendered as six-digit-microsecond RFC 3339. The bytes differ, so the canonical recomputation mismatches. Matching the claim would require re-rendering the timestamp into the drifted form and rehashing, which is a forbidden normalization retry.
